acceptance: A plan (in the PR body) for one supported, documented way to select a deployment from Python config that matches the CLI selector's behavior, with prior art and the rejected alternatives
Registry, credential, DDL-generator, database naming and dry-run recording all resolve the base platform and the selected deployment correctly
The five examples use the supported form and run their dry run with no deprecation warning and the correct mode
lakesail_df_tpch.py works in dry run and the dataframe path passes endpoint and deployment to LakeSailDataFrameAdapter
Tests that fail without the fix for each broken path; CHANGELOG entry; docs for the public option
Deprecated `deployment_mode` keeps working with its warning (migration path)
description: The config-based examples (examples/getting_started/sql/lakesail_tpch.py, lakesail_vs_spark_comparison.py, dataframe/lakesail_df_tpch.py, cloud/tigerdata_tpch.py, cloud/influxdb_tsbs_devops.py dry-run dict ~133) select a deployment with the deprecated `deployment_mode` option. The deprecation (benchbox/core/execution_engine.py:37) points to the CLI `--platform name:mode` selector, which the CLI passes through a private `_deployment_selector` option. Python callers building `DatabaseConfig` have no public, warning-free equivalent: `options={"deployment": ...}` is silently ignored (falls back to self-hosted), and `type="timescaledb:cloud"` breaks registry and credential lookups (keyed on the raw type), puts ':' in database file names, makes `get_ddl_generator` return NoOpDDLGenerator for TimescaleDB, and stops the dry run recording the deployment. Separately, lakesail_df_tpch.py fails in the example dry run with "Unsupported platform: lakesail-df" in either form, and in the orchestrator's dataframe path LakeSailDataFrameAdapter gets endpoint=None and no deployment because options are filtered by PlatformHookRegistry.list_option_specs(type).
